The Norse Greenland page dates the Greenland submission to 1261 (keyframe 1261) and Iceland is dated 1264 (keyframe 1264), so this shape only restates both under Cliopatria's year 1272.

491,243 km2: the 1272 land plus about 62 Finnmark cells (the bbox now reaches 31.1 E) and 25 more in Troms, and Jämtland extended to 296 cells and 16 cells in Västerbotten. The Kingdom page: 'Vardøhus Fortress was erected by Norway in 1306 further east than today's land border', so the northern growth is dated 1306 on the page, eight years before Cliopatria's 1314 (ledger event placed at 1306). Jämtland: the 1314 growth takes the shape from 182 to 296 of the 321 cells of the Natural Earth Jämtland county, which includes Härjedalen. The Härjedalen page says it 'came under the Norwegian king in the Middle Ages, ca. 1100' and the Jämtland page that Jämtland was Norwegian from 1178 until 1645, so this growth is probably Cliopatria drawing late land that the pages call Norwegian earlier; the page gives no year for Västerbotten and the 16 cells there stay unexplained.

489,170 km2: the 1314 land minus four Greenland cells and about one cell in Dalarna. The Kingdom page: 'Norway relinquished all claims to the Kola Peninsula' in the Treaty of Novgorod (1326); Kola was not in the shape. Cliopatria's personal-union relation with Sweden also starts in 1326; the pages date the union from 1319 (Magnus VII).

Repair pass 2026-10-25: Cliopatria's 1333 shape drops the 73 Greenland cells of the 1326 shape (59 inside Greenland) and adds 294 cells (about 74,000 km2) in Värmland (111), Västra Götaland (103), Dalarna (69), Jämtland (4) and Gävleborg (1), none of them dated by any page. Greenland: the Kalmar Union page puts it in Norway 'then including Iceland, Greenland, the Faroe Islands, and the Northern Isles', and the Kingdom page says Greenland 'remained under Norwegian administration until 1814', so the ledger keeps it Norwegian and the drop is Cliopatria's. The Swedish cells: the Erik Magnusson (duke) page says that at the Helsingborg settlement Duke Erik, brother of the designated king Birger, received 'Västergötland, Dalsland, Värmland and Kalmar County', i.e. Swedish provinces (it does not mention Dalarna), and that his son was heir apparent of Norway (Magnus is acclaimed king of Norway in August 1319, Magnus IV page); the Magnus IV page names only Norway, Iceland and Tønsberg as his Norwegian lands; the Kingdom page lists only Jämtland, Herjedalen, Bohuslän, Idre and Särna as Swedish land in the kingdom. Cliopatria's 1333 shape therefore looks like Magnus's composite inheritance, not Norway, and the 1326 shape (same Norwegian land plus Greenland, without those provinces) is used for 1333-1397. 519,922 km2 in Cliopatria; the corrected shape is the 489,170 km2 of 1326-1332. Sources: Kalmar Union, Kingdom of Norway, Erik Magnusson (duke), Magnus IV of Sweden pages.

region.text: the Faroe Islands

ledger.note: 1035: the Faroe Islands become part of the Kingdom of Norway. History of the Faroe Islands page: 'The Faroes became a part of the Kingdom of Norway in 1035.' The page also has Sigmundur Brestisson sent 'to take possession of the islands for Olaf Tryggvason' early in the 11th century, so Norwegian suzerainty may be older; 1035 is the page's year for the kingdom. Cliopatria draws the Faroes from 1040 (Viking settlements row).
1067: the court moves to Bergen. Kingdom page infobox: Bergen 1067-1123 and 1217-1314.

region.text: the Isle of Man and the Hebrides

ledger.note: 1098: Magnus III brings the Hebrides and the Isle of Man under Norway. 'Edgar of Scotland signed the islands over to Magnus III of Norway in 1098' (Treaty of Perth page); the Kingdom page: 'Vassals annexed by King Magnus III in 1098', and Anglesey held briefly until 1099. Drawn as a vassal tint to 1266; which islands the 1098 grant named is the reading.
1123: the court moves to Konungahella (Kungälv). Kingdom page infobox: Konungahella/Kungälv 1123-c. 1150.

1151: the court returns to Nidaros (Trondheim). Kingdom page infobox: "Niðaróss (Trondheim) (997–1016, 1028–1067, 1150–1217)"; Konungahella (Kungälv) (1123 – c. 1150). This dossier starts the span in 1151, the year after the previous capital's span ends.

region.text: Jämtland

ledger.note: 1178: Jämtland is conquered by Norway. Jämtland page: 'Jämtland was conquered by Norway in 1178 and stayed Norwegian for over 450 years until it was ceded to Sweden in 1645', after King Sverre won the Battle of Storsjön; the page adds that it 'never became a fully integrated part of Norway'. Cliopatria draws the change in 1188 (its Jaemtland row ends in 1187).
1217: Bergen is the capital again, as the civil wars end. Kingdom page infobox: Bergen 1217-1314; History of Norway: the wars 'ended in 1217 with the appointment of Håkon Håkonsson'.

region.text: the Norse settlements in Greenland

ledger.note: 1261: the Norse settlements in Greenland subordinate themselves to the Norwegian crown. Norse Greenland page: 'In order to end the constant disputes, the Greenland colony subordinated itself to the Norwegian crown in 1261.' Cliopatria draws them in the Norwegian shape from 1272 and keeps its Norse Greenland row to 1271. The History of Norway page has Haakon IV subjecting Greenland and Iceland (undated for Greenland).

region.text: the Hebrides and the Isle of Man

ledger.note: 1263: Norway and Scotland fight at Largs over the Hebrides and Mann. 'Fought three years before the treaty', inconclusive; Haakon IV dies in Orkney in the winter and Magnus the Law-mender sues for peace.

region.text: Iceland

ledger.note: 1264: Iceland swears to the King of Norway. 'By 1264, all Icelandic chieftains had sworn allegiance to the King of Norway', after the Gamli sáttmáli accepted Haakon IV as king in 1262.

region.text: the Hebrides and the Isle of Man

ledger.note: 1266: the Treaty of Perth ends the dispute over the isles. Signed 2 July 1266 at Perth: Norway recognised Scottish sovereignty over the Hebrides and Mann and kept Shetland and Orkney, for 4,000 marks and an annuity of 100.

region.text: the Hebrides and the Isle of Man

ledger.note: 1266: the Hebrides and the Isle of Man pass to Scotland. 'Norway recognised Scottish sovereignty over the disputed territories, the Hebrides and the Isle of Man'; Scotland confirmed Norway's sovereignty over Shetland and Orkney.

region.text: Finnmark as far east as Cliopatria draws it in 1314

ledger.note: 1306: Norway builds Vardøhus in the far east of Finnmark. 'Vardøhus Fortress was erected by Norway in 1306 further east than today's land border'; the 1251 Novgorod treaty only fixed tribute from Sámi lands. Cliopatria draws the northern growth in 1314.
1314: the capital moves to Oslo. Kingdom page infobox: Ósló 1314-1397 (Bergen to 1314).

1319: the Fairhair line ends and Magnus Eriksson, king of Sweden, is acknowledged king of Norway. 'Elected king of Sweden on 8 July 1319'; in August 1319 acknowledged as 'hereditary king of Norway' at Haugating. Norway page: 'Upon the death of King Haakon V in 1319'. The union with Sweden lasts until 1355.

1343: Haakon VI is made king of Norway. 'At Varberg on 15 August 1343 Haakon would become king of Norway', with Magnus as regent; 'the union between Norway and Sweden would be severed' when Haakon came of age in 1355.

1380: Olaf IV inherits Norway on top of Denmark. 'When Haakon VI died in 1380, Olaf also inherited the crown of Norway' (Kalmar Union page); the list page gives Olav IV 11 Sep 1380-23 Aug 1387. The first Norway-Denmark union.
1387: Margaret becomes regent of Norway and Denmark. 'Margaret became regent of Denmark and Norway when Olaf died in 1387'; the list page gives Olav's death on 23 Aug 1387.
1389: Eric of Pomerania is proclaimed king of Norway. 'After Margaret defeated Albert in 1389, her heir Eric was proclaimed King of Norway' (the list page gives 8 Sep 1389).

region.text: Cliopatria's last Old Kingdom of Norway shape, handed to the Kalmar Union

ledger.note: 1397: the Kalmar Union joins Norway, Denmark and Sweden under one crown. 'His coronation was held in Kalmar on 17 June 1397'; the Kingdom page: disestablished 1397, successor Kalmar Union. Norway's maritime colonies (Iceland, Greenland, the Faroes, Orkney, Shetland) go into the union with it.

wars.name: Battle of Hafrsfjord
wars.outcome: Harald Fairhair's victory over Kjotve the Rich and the western kings, traditionally dated 872; the petty kingdoms are united.
wars.note: The page names Kjotve the Rich (Hrafnsmál), Audbjörn, Solvi Bandy-legs and Arnvid (Egil's Saga) as the defeated and doubts how far the sagas can be trusted.

wars.name: Battle of Svolder

zones.text: Viken, controlled by the Danes as vassals

wars.outcome: Olav Tryggvason is killed; 'the Danes recaptured Norway under Sweyn Forkbeard' and the Lade earls rule the west and Trøndelag.
wars.note: The list page gives Sweyn Forkbeard 1000-1013 de jure and the earls 1000-1015 de facto; the History of Norway page says only 'killed in the Battle of Svolder in 1000'. Svolder was a sea battle; the zone is the land that changed hands.

wars.name: Battle of Stiklestad
wars.outcome: Olaf Haraldsson is killed by the locals; Norway is united again under his son Magnus the Good in 1035.
wars.note: 'Met by the locals in the Battle of Stiklestad, where Olaf was killed'; no change of land in itself, the Canute period 1028-1035 is the ledger's occupation.

wars.name: Magnus III's expedition to the Western Isles

zones.text: the Isle of Man and the Hebrides

wars.outcome: The Hebrides and the Isle of Man come under Norway in 1098 ('Edgar of Scotland signed the islands over to Magnus III'); Anglesey, held briefly, reverts to the Welsh in 1099.
wars.note: Not a named war on the pages; the Kingdom page says only 'Vassals annexed by King Magnus III in 1098'.

wars.name: Norwegian civil wars (era)
belligerents: rival claimants to the Norwegian throne
wars.outcome: 'In 1130, a civil war era broke out over succession to the throne'; the wars 'ended in 1217 with the appointment of Håkon Håkonsson'.
wars.note: A period of dynastic strife, not a territorial war; the page names no parties.

wars.name: Scottish-Norwegian war over the Hebrides (Battle of Largs)

zones.text: the Hebrides and the Isle of Man

wars.outcome: Largs (1263) is inconclusive; Haakon IV dies in Orkney that winter. The Treaty of Perth (2 July 1266) gives the Hebrides and Mann to Scotland and confirms Shetland and Orkney to Norway.
wars.note: The page says Norway claimed its forces were 'not fully committed to battle'; negotiations at Perth ran through 1265 and 1266.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey border in the pages opened; the frontiers of Harald's conquests, the Lade earls' realm, Viken and Jämtland are approximate. Sea and coast edges (Orkney, Shetland, the Faroes) are not in doubt.

The Treaty of Perth (2 July 1266) is a sharp line in the west (Orkney and Shetland to Norway, Hebrides and Mann to Scotland); the 1326 Treaty of Novgorod fixed the north-eastern claims. The Swedish borderlands (Jämtland, Herjedalen, Bohuslän, Idre, Särna) and Greenland stay approximate.

sources.title: Erik Magnusson (duke)
sources.note: Repair pass 2026-10-25: After the Helsingborg settlement (undated) Erik received Västergötland, Dalsland, Värmland and Kalmar County, and northern Halland as a fief from Denmark; his elder brother Birger was the designated king; he married Haakon V's daughter Ingeborg in 1312 and held Kungahälla (Kungälv) against Norway; his son was heir apparent of Norway. Explains where the Swedish provinces in the 1333 shape come from.

sources.title: Bohuslän
sources.note: Repair pass 2026-10-25: Bohuslän (Bahuslen) was a Norwegian county until the Treaty of Roskilde (1658); earliest attested Norwegian affiliation is 11th century; no mention of the Göta älv or Konungahella.

sources.title: Jämtland
sources.note: Repair pass 2026-10-25: "Jämtland was conquered by Norway in 1178 and stayed Norwegian for over 450 years until it was ceded to Sweden in 1645."

sources.title: Härjedalen
sources.note: Repair pass 2026-10-25: "Härjedalen came under the Norwegian king in the Middle Ages, ca. 1100"; ceded to Sweden 1645.

sources.title: Norse Greenland
sources.note: Repair pass 2026-10-25: "the Greenland colony subordinated itself to the Norwegian crown in 1261".

sources.title: History of the Faroe Islands
sources.note: Repair pass 2026-10-25: "The Faroes became a part of the Kingdom of Norway in 1035."; Norwegian supremacy until 1380 (Kalmar Union).

sources.title: Hålogaland
sources.note: Repair pass 2026-10-25: Silent on the year Hålogaland came under Harald; only "Thorolf Kveldulfsson (King of Norway's tax chief starting 872 AD)".

sources.title: Olaf Tryggvason
sources.note: Repair pass 2026-10-25: Reign 995-1000, died at Svolder 1000; silent on Viken returning.

sources.title: Olaf II of Norway
sources.note: Repair pass 2026-10-25: "Olaf returned to Norway in 1015 and declared himself king"; Nesjar 1016 against Earl Sweyn, "hitherto the de facto ruler of Norway"; King 1015-1028; silent on Viken.

notes: Old Kingdom of Norway, written from ten pages (nine for this dossier plus the Icelandic Commonwealth page shared with that dossier). The Kingdom of Norway (872-1397) page is thin (no area, no dates for the acquisitions); the infobox area could not be compared. Unsettled: (1) Start: Cliopatria and the Harald Fairhair page (866 first conquest) against the Norway and Kingdom pages (872). Kept 866. (2) The Isles (Hebrides, Mann): Cliopatria draws them as Norwegian from 990; the pages date only 1098 (Magnus III) and 1266 (Perth); drawn as a vassal tint of the Kingdom of the Isles 1098-1266 (an eu-11 dossier). (3) Viken: the list page has the Lade earl ruling 'except Viken' 970-995; Cliopatria restores it in 980. (4) 1046-1055: Cliopatria's Norway-Denmark row contains all of Norway; a new Norway keyframe was written, the pages do not show Norway united with Denmark after 1047; norway-denmark (another part) should settle which is drawn. (5) Repair pass 2026-10-25: Cliopatria's 1333-1401 shapes drop Greenland and add about 74,000 km2 of Värmland, Västra Götaland and Dalarna. The Kalmar Union and Kingdom pages keep Greenland in Norway, and the Erik Magnusson (duke) page makes Västergötland, Dalsland and Värmland Duke Erik's lands, so keyframes 1333, 1344, 1363 and 1395 are corrected to Cliopatria's 1326 shape (Greenland kept, the fief removed). The Bohuslän page: a Norwegian county until 1658. (6) The end: 1397 on both pages against Cliopatria's 1401; the Cliopatria Kalmar Union row starts 1402. (7) Personal unions: Magnus VII is king of Norway from August 1319 (Magnus page), the union with Sweden ends 1355 although Cliopatria's relation rows run 1326-1362 and 1363-1374; Olaf IV unites Norway and Denmark in 1380 against Cliopatria's relation 1385-1401. The ledger has no union event type, so these are rename events. (8) Iceland: all chieftains sworn by 1264 (Icelandic Commonwealth page), the Old Covenant 1262; Cliopatria's Commonwealth runs to 1271 and Norway's shape includes Iceland from 1272. (9) Greenland: the Norse Greenland page dates the submission to 1261 (confidence 3; Cliopatria draws it in 1272); a new keyframe 1261-1263 carries it. Cliopatria's Norse Greenland row (1072-1271, 1363-1384) overlaps; norse-greenland must be settled by its own dossier. (10) Kola: the Kingdom page says Norway 'relinquished all claims to the Kola Peninsula' in 1326; no event was written because Kola was never in the shape and the gazetteer has no Kola region. (11) The 1251 treaty with Novgorod and the 1323 Treaty of Nöteborg appear on the Kingdom page; the Magnus page makes Nöteborg a Sweden-Novgorod treaty. Gazetteer names used that do not resolve: none expected; the region names Viken and Hålogaland are written as unions of Natural Earth admin-1 units. Repair pass 2026-10-25 (reviewer's findings): (a) Greenland and the Swedish provinces, see (5); (b) capital_move events added for the returns to Nidaros in 998, 1029 and 1151: the Kingdom infobox dates them (Niðaróss 997–1016, 1028–1067, 1150–1217), so they are not inferred; (c) Jämtland moved from 1188 to 1178 (Jämtland page, confidence 3), keyframe 1178-1187 added; Härjedalen page: Norwegian 'ca. 1100', no shape written (the gazetteer has no Härjedalen); (d) Faroes moved from 1040 to 1035 (History of the Faroe Islands page, confidence 3), keyframe 1035-1039 added; (e) Hålogaland 870, Viken 995 and 1015 reopened on the Hålogaland, Olaf Tryggvason and Olaf II pages: all silent on the Viken return and on the Hålogaland year, so they stay at confidence 1; (f) Konungahella (Kungälv, 11.97 E 57.87 N) lies about 25 km outside every Cliopatria shape of the kingdom; the Bohuslän page makes the whole county Norwegian but does not mention the Göta älv, and the gazetteer has no Bohuslän or Kungälv, so the shape was left as drawn.
